script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for August 12. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
A car going 60 mph isn't accelerating if it stays at 60.  A car going 10 mph but speeding up to 20 is accelerating.  Acceleration isn't speed—it's change in speed.

Acceleration is change in speed over time. It's the rate of change. This meta-level thinking—not just what, but how it's changing—is powerful in physics and in life. Positive acceleration speeds you up.  Negative acceleration (deceleration) slows you down.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: What matters isn't just where you are or how fast you're going, but whether you're accelerating or decelerating.  Watch your trajectory.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Acceleration Check - Gaining or Losing Momentum?.

Here's your activity: Pick a skill or goal. Is your rate of progress increasing (acceleration), steady (coasting), or decreasing (deceleration)? If decelerating, what could reignite acceleration? New challenges, different methods, renewed motivation? This helps you evaluate rate of progress change.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about speeding up and slowing down can be applied to acceleration check - gaining or losing momentum?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
